# Paths OUTSIDE backend/ that must run the backend test suite (#821).
#
# ci-backend-relevant.sh checks these prefixes BEFORE its deny-list, so a
# subtree can be denied wholesale (agent/, appliance/, .github/) while the
# specific files the suite actually depends on keep running it.
#
# One prefix per line; a line ending in "/" matches the whole subtree,
# otherwise it is a plain prefix (in practice: an exact file). Blank lines
# and "#" comments are ignored.
#
# This file is enforced against reality in both directions by
# backend/tests/test_ci_backend_relevant.py:
#   - every entry must exist on disk (no stale carve-outs), and
#   - every repo-root escape in backend/tests (a ``parents[2+]`` read) must
#     be covered by an entry here — so a new cross-boundary read that nobody
#     declared fails the suite loudly instead of silently losing coverage.
# Editing THIS file runs the suite too (it lives under .github/scripts/).

# test_spatium_console.py loads the console script directly — 52 tests.
# test_appliance_join_auto_retry.py parses spatium-cluster-join's
# classify_join_failure and pins each message it can emit against the
# backend's permanent-vs-transient markers, so rewording the runner has to
# run the suite that would otherwise silently start misclassifying.
appliance/mkosi.extra/usr/local/bin/

# test_appliance_firewall_render.py imports the renderer by path, and
# test_outbound_hosts_documented.py (#1353) scans this package for outbound
# hosts — as it does the three below.
agent/supervisor/spatium_supervisor/

# test_outbound_hosts_documented.py (#1353) scans every shipped agent package
# for hostname and public-IP literals and requires each in docs/PRIVACY.md.
# #976 scanned backend/app only, and the connection it then missed was in
# agent code — PowerDNS's hardcoded ALIAS resolvers. Without these an
# agent-only PR adding an outbound host would go green without the guard.
# The agents' tests/ directories are not shipped, not scanned, and stay
# denied. A new agent package fails test_every_agent_package_is_scanned
# until it is added both there and here.
agent/dhcp/spatium_dhcp_agent/
agent/dns/spatium_dns_agent/
agent/looking-glass/spatium_lg_agent/

# test_dhcp_packet_loss.py (#980) pins the agent's metric column names
# against the ingest model's fields. That model does not forbid extra keys —
# deliberately, so a newer agent posting a field an older control plane has
# never heard of loses the field rather than having the whole sample 422'd
# mid-upgrade — which means a TYPO is equally silent: the column would stay
# NULL forever and every surface would report "loss not measured" on a fleet
# that is measuring fine. agent/ is denied wholesale, so without this
# carve-out the one edit that can break the boundary would not run the test
# guarding it.
agent/dhcp/spatium_dhcp_agent/metrics.py

# test_openapi_export.py runs the release-asset exporter (#903) and pins
# that its output still goes through app.openapi()'s wrapper.
scripts/export_openapi.py

# test_merge_test_durations.py (#1019) loads the shard-durations merge the
# aggregator runs, and pins that a partial or malformed shard file is refused
# rather than published as the file the next release balances the shards with.
scripts/merge_test_durations.py

# test_lint_versions.py (#975) loads the version-pin manifest guard and pins
# its negative cases — a renamed pinned_in path erroring rather than skipping,
# and an exact occurrence count catching a partial bump. scripts/ is not
# denied, so the gate would run the suite anyway; the entry exists because the
# scan test above requires every declared read to be covered here, and a
# future widening of the deny-list must not silently drop this one.
scripts/lint_versions.py

# test_lint_workflow_shell.py (#1036) loads the workflow shell-status guard
# and pins it against the real pre-fix trivy-scheduled.yml body, plus the
# false-positive case that made the first draft unusable (a `set -e` inside a
# function is not evidence that -e is on at an arbitrary later line).
scripts/lint_workflow_shell.py

# test_lint_image_upgrades.py (#1088) loads the shipped-image package-upgrade
# guard and pins its negative cases — including the one that decides whether
# the linter checks anything at all: a nightly.yml whose images heredoc has
# been restructured must RAISE, not find zero images and report success.
scripts/lint_image_upgrades.py

# test_release_version_script.py (#1226) loads the release workflow's tag
# helper and pins the decisions it makes for release.yml: which tags may be
# published, the previous release across the CalVer → SemVer switch, and
# whether a tag becomes :latest.
scripts/release_version.py

# test_trivy_scan_script.py (#1272) runs the `make trivy` loop against a
# stubbed docker and pins that a scan which never ran reads as SCAN FAILED,
# never as FINDINGS — and reads the Makefile to pin that the target still
# calls it, with the DB cache outside the checkout.
scripts/trivy-scan.sh
Makefile

# test_zone_name_scope.py (#986) loads the release-prep TLD regenerator and
# pins that it uses the PRODUCT's payload guard rather than a second copy —
# so a PR that gives the script its own parser has to run the test that says
# it must not. The script is also the only writer of the bundled TLD list.
scripts/refresh_iana_tlds.py

# test_outbound_hosts_documented.py (#976) asserts every hostname literal in
# backend/app is documented in the privacy statement. docs/ is denied
# wholesale, so without this carve-out a PR that quietly deletes a row from
# PRIVACY.md would go green — the one edit that must run the guard.
docs/PRIVACY.md

# The gate machinery itself: the script, this manifest, and the tests that
# pin them. Any edit here must run the suite that contains those tests.
.github/scripts/

# The workflow that orchestrates the shards. Not a "read", but a change to
# how the suite is invoked should exercise the suite. Other workflows are
# denied — none of them runs backend tests.
.github/workflows/ci.yml

# test_trivy_scheduled_report.py (#1095) pins the weekly scan's report shape:
# JSON rendering rather than a byte-capped table, and rc=1 validated against
# the report before it is called "findings". Both failures are invisible in a
# green run — the workflow succeeds and files an issue naming no CVE — so the
# edit that would reintroduce them must run the test that says it must not.
.github/workflows/trivy-scheduled.yml

# test_trivy_pr_lanes.py (#1093) pins that every PR-time image lane busts its
# cached package layer and routes its verdict through trivy-gate.sh rather
# than Trivy's own exit code. Listed exactly rather than as a
# ".github/workflows/build-" prefix because test_manifest_entries_exist_on_disk
# requires every entry to name something real — a prefix that matches nothing
# is how a stale carve-out hides. The test itself globs, so a fifth lane is
# covered the day it lands; add it here too so editing it runs that test.
.github/workflows/build-dns-images.yml
.github/workflows/build-dhcp-images.yml
.github/workflows/build-looking-glass-images.yml
.github/workflows/build-supervisor-image.yml

# The two shipped nginx templates (#972). `backend/tests/test_e911_held.py`
# asserts both carry a `location /held` block: the HELD endpoint is mounted at
# the application root rather than under /api/, so without one it falls through
# to the SPA `location /` and a PBX asking where a phone is gets index.html
# with a 200 — unreachable in production while every backend test passes.
# Editing either must therefore run the suite that contains that assertion.
frontend/default.conf.template
charts/spatiumddi/templates/frontend-tls-config.yaml
